title: Architecture-aware kernel serialization and pin policy for MHA/GQA/MoE
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement an architecture-aware kernel artifact format, signing/serialization pipeline, and a deterministic model->kernel pinning policy for MHA, GQA and MoE variants. The deliverable should enable automated publishing of performance profiles and safe rollouts of kernel updates tied to specific model versions.

Background: We currently have several independent kernel builds and per-model heuristic routing. As we onboard more models with heterogeneous attention (MHA, GQA) and router-based MoE, we need a reproducible way to: 1) serialize kernel binaries and metadata, 2) publish performance/compatibility profiles, 3) pin model versions to tested kernel profiles, and 4) provide an automated fallback when an update regresses latency or correctness. This ticket covers spec, implementation, tests, and the first pilot with the GQA-XS and MoE-Base families.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel artifact format (binary + metadata protobuf) documented and agreed in design doc
Onboarding pipeline produces signed artifacts uploaded to artifact registry S3 bucket with semantic versioning
Compatibility matrix generated per model architecture (MHA/GQA/MoE) and published alongside profiles
Model-to-kernel pin stored in the runtime registry and exposed via admin API
Automated perf and correctness CI gates for publishing new kernel profiles
Canary rollout mechanism validated on dedicated capacity with automatic rollback on QoS regressions
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created. Initial scoping meeting with Runtime, Compiler and Onboarding teams. Action: draft artifact schema.

2025-02-14: Prototype metadata protobuf sketched (see design doc). Decided to include: arch tag, compiler flags, sequence-length-optimized-ids, KV-cache version, feature-flags, checksum and signature reference.
2025-02-20: Implemented serialization CLI (kernel-pack) proof-of-concept. CLI bundles kernel binary + metadata.json and produces tar.gz with checksum. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4123
2025-02-25: Compiler team ran baseline perf on MHA-Base and GQA-XS with kernel-pack artifacts. Observed 3-5% variance; added mandatory perf harness step in pipeline.

2025-03-01: Design review with Security and SRE. Security requested signed artifacts and an ACLed artifact bucket. SRE suggested tagging artifacts with expected latency SLO vectors for canary evaluation.
2025-03-03: API changes drafted to expose model->kernel pins (admin route). Split PRs created: runtime registry change (PR #4189) and artifact publishing job (PR #4192).
technical_decisions: Use protobuf for artifact metadata to avoid fragile JSON schema drift
Adopt semantic versioning for kernel profiles: MAJOR.FEAT.PATCH where MAJOR bumps on ABI changes, FEAT for micro-optimizations, PATCH for fixes
Store artifacts in an ACLed S3 bucket (artifacts.redwood-inference/runtime-kernels) and mirror to internal registry for quick access
Require signed manifests (RSA-4096) from compiler team before publishing; runtime validates signatures at pull time
Define compatibility levels: ABI, KV-cache, attention-variant flags. Incompatibilities block automatic pin migration
Default pinning policy: model_version -> kernel_profile exact match. If no exact match, allow compatible-variant fallback with telemetry-enabled approval
Perf gates: new kernel profile must pass regression <+/-3% latency and correctness bit-exact (or tolerated tolerance matrix) on standardized input suites
Fallback behavior: on detected QoS regression during rollout, automatic revert to last pinned kernel and open incident ticket with collected traces
testing_plan: Unit tests for kernel-pack serialization (checksum and signature verification)
Integration test: publish artifact -> runtime pulls -> verifies signature -> loads kernel for small inference run
Perf CI: run nightly benchmark suite for MHA/GQA/MoE families covering seq-len 32/128/512/2048; compare against baseline pins
Correctness CI: run reference prompt set (existing evals repo) to ensure numerical consistency within tolerated deltas
Chaos test: simulate partial artifact unavailability and validate fallback paths and alerts
Canary test: deploy new profile to 2% of dedicated capacity for 24h and monitor latency, error-rate, and quality regressions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): publish first signed artifacts for GQA-XS and MoE-Base to staging registry
Phase 1 (canary): route 2% traffic for each model family on dedicated capacity, monitor for 48h
Phase 2 (gradual): if canary stable, increase to 25% then 100% on non-critical tenants over 7 days
Phase 3 (pinning): update model->kernel pin in registry and record release notes; enable audit logging
Rollback: automatic on metrics regression or manual via admin API; create postmortem and attach traces
notes: Follow-ups: 1) add automated telemetry alerts for subtle quality regressions tied to semantic evals; 2) extend artifact schema to include quantization profile metadata; 3) plan private-deployment (VPC) signing key rotation guidance. Coordinate with PM for documentation and customer-facing migration notes.
